claims.text: Nested sampling using unbiased phase-space integration can accurately and efficiently determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed simulation begins with 10,000 live configurations.
Energy thresholds are decremented by approximately 1–2% per iteration.
The simulation is performed under constant-pressure, controlled-temperature conditions near the experimental melting point.
Nested sampling accesses the full free-energy landscape of the alloy.
The sampled landscape aggregates contributions from all stable and metastable configurations.
Aggregation of stable and metastable configurations mediates the observed entropy and volume changes.
Nested sampling exhaustively integrates the partition function over the complete free-energy landscape.
Integration over the complete landscape captures the disordered, multicomponent character of high-entropy alloys.
Capturing configurational entropy and heterogeneity enables extraction of latent heat and volume change at melting.
Predicted melting temperatures will agree with precise experiments to within approximately ±1–2%.
Predicted fusion enthalpies and entropies will agree with precise experiments to within approximately ±1–2%.
The method will accurately capture volume change at melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
Differential scanning calorimetry, conventional CALPHAD, and molecular dynamics have limited sensitivity and universality for complex high-entropy-alloy free-energy landscapes.
The approach is applicable when the free-energy landscape is not overwhelmingly dominated by nonequilibrium metastable states.
The approach is primarily effective at low or near-atmospheric pressures.
The approach is primarily effective for compositions without extreme atomic-scale phase separation.
Extremely complex alloys may suffer from sampling insufficiency and prohibitive computational scaling.
Validation should compare simulated melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting volume change against independent DSC and XRD measurements under matched conditions.
The method is falsified if melting temperature or any specified fusion parameter deviates from experiment by more than ±2%.

contradictions.description: The mediator and mechanism claim access to all configurations and exhaustive integration over the complete landscape, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges possible sampling insufficiency. The absolute completeness claims are therefore inconsistent with the stated limitation.
